lessons.title: Hello, panel
lessons.objective: Send one explicit text value to one explicit display sink.
lessons.prose: A panel is a bounded assembly of named nodes and cords. Run this one before changing it.
hints: The literal node produces text on its value port.
The display node consumes text on its text port.
lessons.solution: Connect greeting.value to output.text with the declared bounded cord.

accessibility.non_audio: The visible text output is the complete result.

lessons.title: Pull the cord
lessons.objective: Observe that a required input is not satisfied by a nearby node.
lessons.prose: Remove a cord on purpose. A useful diagnostic names the missing boundary instead of guessing a connection.
hints: The output node has one required input.
A node declaration does not create a connection.
lessons.solution: Restore the bounded cord from greeting.value to output.text.

accessibility.non_audio: The structured diagnostic is available as text.

lessons.title: Change the message
lessons.objective: Edit semantic configuration while preserving the same panel structure.
lessons.prose: Change the literal value, then select and move its faceplate. Source semantics and presentation are separate identities.
hints: Only the value configuration needs to change.
Moving a selected node does not rewrite source.
lessons.solution: Set greeting.value to the desired text and retain its explicit cord.

accessibility.non_audio: The output and source selection do not depend on color or sound.

lessons.title: Nothing up our sleeves
lessons.objective: Take the exact authored panel home and run it with the canonical command.
lessons.prose: Download preserves the real source you just ran. The same source is checked with conduct --check and executed with conduct --run outside the Tour.
hints: Use Download after editing.
The command shown is the normal conduit command, not a Tour command.
lessons.solution: Download the source, then run conduct --check lesson.panel followed by conduct --run lesson.panel.

accessibility.non_audio: The executable result is represented by text output and canonical commands.

lessons.title: More than one port
lessons.objective: Patch two independently named inputs instead of treating a node like universal stdin.
lessons.prose: The display panel exports left and right jacks. Each jack retains its own typed boundary and each incoming cord has a separate finite budget.
hints: The exported names are display.left and display.right.
Each source needs its own cord.
lessons.solution: Connect left.value to display.left and right.value to display.right with separate bounded cords.

accessibility.non_audio: Both named inputs produce ordered visible text.

lessons.title: Direction matters
lessons.objective: See a wrong-direction cord rejected at the exact destination port.
lessons.prose: Ports are directional contracts. An output cannot stand in for an input, even when both nodes produce the same text type.
hints: Look at the port after the arrow.
A literal node only exposes an output port.
lessons.solution: Connect an outgoing port to a receiving port, such as the value and text ports declared by std/literal and display/text.

accessibility.non_audio: The direction failure is exposed as a structured text diagnostic.

runnability.reason: the authored lesson intentionally has no resolvable exact plan

lessons.title: Fan-out is a choice
lessons.objective: Choose an explicit bounded fan-out contract when one value must reach more than one sink.
lessons.prose: The tee contract makes duplication and branch pressure explicit. Its receiving value port and outgoing left and right ports are visible in source, and each sink receives one value.
lessons.source:
panel 0

node greeting : std/literal {
    value = "Fan out.\n"
}
node messages : std/text/lines {
    maximum_line_bytes = 1024
    maximum_retained_prefix_bytes = 1024
}
node split : conduit.std/tee {
    mode = "coupled"
}
node left_text : std/text/join {
    separator = ""
    maximum_items = 8
    maximum_item_bytes = 1024
    maximum_separator_bytes = 64
    maximum_output_bytes = 4096
}
node right_text : std/text/join {
    separator = ""
    maximum_items = 8
    maximum_item_bytes = 1024
    maximum_separator_bytes = 64
    maximum_output_bytes = 4096
}
node first : display/text
node second : display/text

cord greeting.value -> messages.text {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord messages.line -> split.value {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord split.left -> left_text.item {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord split.right -> right_text.item {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord left_text.text -> first.text {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 4096
    max_queued_bytes = 4096
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord right_text.text -> second.text {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 4096
    max_queued_bytes = 4096
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
hints: The tee's coupled mode admits one value only when both outgoing branches can accept it.
Each cord declares its own finite capacity and pressure rule.
lessons.solution: Split the finite text batch into line values, tee messages.line into two explicit branches, join each finite branch, then connect both joined text values to distinct display ports.

accessibility.non_audio: Both delivered values appear as text output.

lessons.title: Types mean promises

    value = "Adapt me.\n"

node adapter : example/text-adapter

cord source.value -> adapter.text {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord adapter.text -> sink.text {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
hints: The adapter name is not registered.
A real adapter needs its own contract and implementation.
lessons.solution: Replace the invented adapter with a declared compatible implementation, such as text/uppercase for this text exercise.

accessibility.non_audio: The missing implementation is reported as a structured text diagnostic.

lessons.title: Put a panel in a panel

lessons.prose: The composite exports only the ports it chooses. Its internal uppercase worker remains an implementation detail while the boundary remains substitutable for a primitive node.
lessons.source:
panel 0

composite example/uppercase {
    node worker : text/uppercase
    export > text = worker.text
    export value > = worker.text
}

node source : std/literal {
    value = "boundary"
}
node transform : example/uppercase
node sink : display/text

cord source.value -> transform.text {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord transform.value -> sink.text {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
hints: The composite has an input export and an output export.
The top-level cords connect to the composite boundary, not directly to worker.
lessons.solution: Keep the worker behind exported in/out ports, then connect the literal to transform and transform to the sink.

accessibility.non_audio: The uppercase transformation is visible as text output and source structure.

hints: Outer cords name faceplate.text and faceplate.result.

lessons.title: Patchbay observes Patchbay
lessons.objective: Inspect the root patchbay.panel graph inside Patchbay itself.
lessons.prose: Patchbay is an authored .panel graph. Witness its composite surfaces (authoring, presentation, observation) and inspect its own logical and expanded topology.
lessons.source:
panel 0

composite patchbay/authoring {
    node editor : text/uppercase
    node parser : text/uppercase
    export > source = editor.text
    export parsed > = parser.text
    cord editor.text -> parser.text {
        capacity = 1
        max_value_bytes = 1024
        max_queued_bytes = 1024
        low_watermark = 0
        high_watermark = 1
        pressure = block
    }
}

composite patchbay/presentation {
    node layout : text/uppercase
    node canvas : text/uppercase
    export > positions = layout.text
    export rendered > = canvas.text
    cord layout.text -> canvas.text {
        capacity = 1
        max_value_bytes = 1024
        max_queued_bytes = 1024
        low_watermark = 0
        high_watermark = 1
        pressure = block
    }
}

composite patchbay/observation {
    node resolver : text/uppercase
    node evidence_feed : text/uppercase
    export > plan = resolver.text
    export telemetry > = evidence_feed.text
    cord resolver.text -> evidence_feed.text {
        capacity = 1
        max_value_bytes = 1024
        max_queued_bytes = 1024
        low_watermark = 0
        high_watermark = 1
        pressure = block
    }
}

node nav_selection : std/literal {
    value = "tour/meta-lesson\n"

node presentation_surface : patchbay/presentation

    max_value_bytes = 1024

    high_watermark = 4
    pressure = block

cord authoring_surface.parsed -> presentation_surface.positions {
    capacity = 4
    max_value_bytes = 4096
    max_queued_bytes = 16384
    low_watermark = 1

lessons.title: Typed text formatting
lessons.objective: Format bounded text, split logical lines, and join a finite item stream while inspecting the exact graph and ordered evidence story.
lessons.prose: The formatter emits one typed text value. Lines removes LF or CRLF delimiters without depending on implementation chunks; join retains a finite bounded item stream and emits one ordered result.
hints: The template and values inputs have different exact value types.
Select a scenario, edit its typed node configuration, and rerun.
Timeline controls reveal existing evidence; they do not execute the graph.
lessons.solution: Connect std/text and std/format-values producers to the formatter's exact inputs, then connect its std/text output to a consumer.

accessibility.non_audio: Every graph event is also an ordered table row with sequence, tick, subject, event, pressure, occupancy, and terminal cause.
accessibility.keyboard: Native controls plus Space to play and ArrowRight to step while the execution story has focus.
accessibility.color_independent: Event labels, lane names, marker shapes, table text, and graph selection duplicate every color cue.

library.summary: Bounded format, lines, and join nodes turn typed text into exact finite graph operations.
library.what: Format substitutes typed values; lines emits delimiter-free LF/CRLF logical lines; join inserts one separator between a finite ordered item set.
library.when: Use them when panel data must become bounded text, line-oriented values, or one finite combined value without provider-specific conventions.
library.wrong: Malformed placeholders, invalid UTF-8, oversized lines or items, an open-ended join input, and retained or output overflow terminate with exact codes.

scenarios.title: Standalone success
scenarios.explanation: Format one named value and send the resulting text directly to display.

scenarios.title: Composed with uppercase
scenarios.explanation: Feed the formatter's typed text output into another standard text node before display.

scenarios.title: Missing named value
scenarios.explanation: The authored template requests a name that the typed values collection does not contain.

scenarios.title: Cancelled before first step
scenarios.explanation: Ask the exact runtime to apply deterministic abort cancellation before any node step.

scenarios.title: Logical lines joined in order
scenarios.explanation: Split LF and CRLF text into the same ordered logical values, including an empty line, then join the finite stream.

scenarios.title: Formatted text becomes logical lines
scenarios.explanation: Format typed values into CRLF/LF text, split it into lines, and visibly preserve the same ordering through a finite join.

lessons.title: Bounded flow control
lessons.objective: Run the canonical tee, merge, zip, gate, and select contracts and inspect the exact ordering, pressure, retained-state, and terminal facts that make their behavior portable.
lessons.prose: These nodes shape a stream without inventing a universal value type. This lesson uses their exact std/text instantiations, capacity-one block pressure, finite retained state, and explicit terminal policies.
hints: Select one standalone scenario before changing its supported configuration.
Capacity and pressure belong to each cord; ordering and retained-state policy belong to the selected node contract.
The timeline is a projection of bounded evidence and never changes the resolved plan.
lessons.solution: Use the canonical conduit.std identities, exact typed ports, supported finite configuration, and capacity-one blocking cords; inspect the resolved plan before treating the timeline as evidence.

accessibility.non_audio: An ordered text table names sequence, node, port, pressure result, occupancy, retained-value count, ordering decision, terminal input, and final cause.
accessibility.keyboard: Native controls plus Space to play and ArrowRight to step while the ordered flow story has focus.
accessibility.color_independent: Port labels, branch numbers, ordering ordinals, terminal words, and table text duplicate every graph color.

library.summary: Five canonical structural nodes provide bounded fan-out, merge, pairing, admission, and selection.
library.what: Tee duplicates one value to two branches; merge chooses available inputs round-robin; zip emits complete pairs; gate admits data only while open; select consumes only its active input.
library.when: Use these nodes when stream topology needs an explicit, inspectable structural policy instead of hidden callback or host-channel behavior.
library.wrong: Legacy flow/* identities, duplicate port IDs, wake-order races, partial coupled publication, unbounded retention, implicit dropping, and fabricated terminal success fail closed.
expected_evidence: exact contract, implementation, artifact, and port bindings
capacity-one block pressure and queue occupancy
round-robin input ordinal or control-priority decision
bounded retained-value usage and one exact terminal cause

scenarios.title: Coupled tee
scenarios.semantics: Both branches reserve in one scheduler transaction; block pressure rolls the whole step back.

scenarios.title: Round-robin merge
scenarios.semantics: One available value is chosen per input ordinal cycle; completion drains both inputs.

scenarios.title: Pairwise zip
scenarios.semantics: At most one value per side is retained; both outputs publish in one scheduler transaction.

scenarios.title: Controlled gate
scenarios.semantics: Control is processed before data; closed block mode retains values only in bounded input queues.

scenarios.title: Controlled select
scenarios.semantics: Control is processed before the selected input; inactive block mode leaves the other queue untouched.

scenarios.title: Select then tee
scenarios.semantics: The selected exact text value reaches both coupled branches with the same handle and terminal cause.

lessons.title: Bounded value facts, clocks, and feedback
lessons.objective: Run real text nodes, then see how the exact plan admits only bounded value facts, explicit clock conversion, and finite feedback.
lessons.prose: The panel remains ordinary source. Its exact plan decides whether a cord may carry correlation, provenance, sensitivity, and timestamps. Clock integers compare only through a fresh conversion with uncertainty. A cycle starts only when one edge is an admitted finite delay or state boundary.
hints: Edit message.value and rerun; the nodes still execute under the exact bounded plan.
An authorized optional field may remain absent. The runtime never invents correlation or provenance.
Remove the finite boundary from the cycle profile and admission fails before any node starts.
lessons.solution: Keep each cord finite, authorize only the value facts its consumers need, bind cross-clock comparisons explicitly, and break every intentional cycle with one finite state or delay boundary.

accessibility.non_audio: The graph is paired with an ordered table containing sequence, tick, clock domain, uncertainty, pressure, retained state, cancellation, errors, and terminal cause.
accessibility.keyboard: Native controls plus Space to play and ArrowRight to step while the ordered execution story has focus.
accessibility.color_independent: Labels, bounds, marker shapes, and ordered text duplicate envelope, clock, state, pressure, error, and terminal colors.

platform.what: The current exact plan pins every permitted envelope field and byte ceiling, every clock conversion and uncertainty claim, and every finite feedback boundary.
platform.when: Use these facts when values need traceable identity or time across a cord, when clocks differ, or when a real graph intentionally feeds state back.
platform.wrong: Unbounded metadata, sensitivity widening, unlisted clocks, stale conversion, impersonated correlation, zero retention, and cycles without boundaries are rejected before consumer visibility or execution.
authoritative_story: plan envelope authorization and queue bytes
clock domain plus converted uncertainty interval
ordered value acceptance and pressure evidence
feedback initialization and retained-state ceiling
cancellation, exact error, and terminal evidence

lessons.title: Finite leases and honest effect commits
lessons.objective: Run a representative panel while inspecting the exact lease, commit, retry, and cleanup facts that must exist before a host effect mutates anything.
lessons.prose: Authority permits an effect, but it does not reserve a resource or make retries exactly once. The current plan pins the holder, run, epoch, capacity, expiry, commit boundary, lost-ack policy, and finite cleanup disposition.
lessons.source:
panel 0

node source : std/literal {
    value = "Leased effect boundaries stay explicit.\n"
}
node emphasize : text/uppercase
node output : display/text

cord source.value -> emphasize.text {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 128
    max_queued_bytes = 128
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord emphasize.text -> output.text {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 128
    max_queued_bytes = 128
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
hints: The editable panel remains ordinary source; lease and commit facts belong to its resolved exact plan.
A host loss after commit but before acknowledgement is commit-unknown, never success.
Cancellation remains pending until cleanup or reconciliation reaches a finite disposition.
lessons.solution: Pin a finite run-scoped lease, recheck authority and lease at every use, reserve evidence before mutation, and use the domain's exact commit and cleanup profile.

accessibility.non_audio: Lease identity, bounds, fault point, commit state, cleanup disposition, and terminal result are presented as ordered text.
accessibility.keyboard: Native controls plus Space to play and ArrowRight to step while the ordered execution story has focus.
accessibility.color_independent: Labels and ordered text duplicate every admission, commit, unknown, cleanup, and terminal color.

platform.what: The current exact plan pins one finite resource lease beside its resource binding and one domain-owned commit profile beside each effect authority.
platform.when: Use these contracts whenever an operation holds scarce capacity, mutates an external domain, can lose its acknowledgement, or needs cancellation cleanup.
platform.wrong: Wrong holder, run, epoch, resource, time, evidence, or release generation fails closed. Unknown commit cannot be reported as success or upgraded to global exactly once.
authoritative_story: plan lease holder, run, epoch, scope, reservation, and expiry
fresh authority plus lease admission before provider mutation
domain commit boundary and acknowledgement disposition
same-key retry or reconciliation after unknown commit
finite cancellation cleanup, release sequence, and escalation

lessons.prose: A fast benchmark and a fresh host report are observations. The current plan admits a hard deadline only from exact enforcement evidence on the named clock with every required resource category reserved.

    value = "Deadline guarantees stay separate from measurements.\n"

cord source.value -> emphasize.text {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 128
    max_queued_bytes = 128
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord emphasize.text -> output.text {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 128
    max_queued_bytes = 128
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
lessons.expected_display: DEADLINE GUARANTEES STAY SEPARATE FROM MEASUREMENTS.

validation.value: DEADLINE GUARANTEES STAY SEPARATE FROM MEASUREMENTS.

hints: Edit message.value and rerun; the ordinary nodes stay distinct from the plan workload declaration.
A Linux timing sample and browser availability remain observations even when they look fast.
Callbacks, foreign queues, and transition overlap must fit the same finite admission.
lessons.solution: Declare every category finite or unsupported, pin one clock and deadline, and require fresh exact enforcement evidence before calling the result hard.

accessibility.non_audio: The graph is paired with ordered text for declaration, observation, admission, usage, deadline, overload, and terminal evidence.
accessibility.keyboard: Native controls plus Space to play and ArrowRight to step while the ordered execution story has focus.
accessibility.color_independent: Guarantee labels, resource values, reason codes, and ordered text duplicate every admission and deadline color.

platform.what: The current exact plan pins the workload class, finite-or-unsupported categories, clock, deadline, jitter, host observation, and exact enforcement evidence separately.
platform.when: Use hard admission only when the selected host can enforce the declared reservation and deadline. Use measured or best-effort profiles for observations that do not grant that authority.
platform.wrong: Benchmarks, stale reports, wrong clocks, hidden callbacks, uncounted overlap, implicit priority escalation, and best-effort downgrade reported as hard success fail closed.
authoritative_story: plan workload classification and finite-or-unsupported resource categories
fresh capability evidence, named clock, deadline, and jitter admission
ordered work, callback, foreign-queue, and transition-overlap accounting
measured Linux and best-effort browser observations remain non-authoritative
overload, missed deadline, exact reason code, and terminal evidence

lessons.title: A provider is more than a matching label
lessons.objective: Run one semantic graph while comparing exact provider chains across Linux, browser/WASM, firmware, deterministic, and describe-only profiles.
lessons.prose: Discovery tells you which contracts and extensions a host understands. Execution additionally needs a fresh available provider, complete satisfaction proof, passing behavioral conformance, exact artifacts, finite bounds, and an explicit adapter when custom type identities differ.
lessons.source:
panel 0

# The graph stays semantic. A host profile may bind exact providers for these

lessons.title: Imports name meaning; plans provide machines
lessons.objective: Compare a friendly source alias with its exact canonical contract identity, then distinguish successful offline import checking from provider availability.
lessons.prose: The alias split is source-local; conduit.dev/std/tee is the package-owned semantic identity and its descriptor hash pins the exact contract: imports name the part; the plan determines whether a particular machine can provide it. Import resolution reads only the supplied contract-package bytes and lock, never a URL, package registry, installer, grant, or provider selector.
lessons.source:
panel 3

import conduit.dev/std/{tee as split}

# The import can check offline while this selected host has no provider.
node branch : split
hints: Select split to reveal conduit.dev/std/tee and its pinned descriptor hash.
Switch to the missing-export scenario to see deterministic CND-IPK-004 source-span evidence.
Notice that successful import checking adds no installed provider, host grant, or authority.
lessons.solution: Supply the immutable package artifact and exact lock to the checker, retain the alias only for presentation, and let later exact planning decide whether current host facts permit a provider binding.
